source.title: LETToT: Label-Free Evaluation of Large Language Models On Tourism Using Expert Tree-of-Thought
source.authors: Ruiyan Qi; Congding Wen; Weibo Zhou; Jiwei Li; Shangsong Liang; Lingbo Li

record.tranche_reason: The study compares tourism-task scores across models of different stated sizes and claims scaling persists in this domain, but it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling curves.
record.gate_note: The tourism prompt-optimization results and expert-ToT scoring results are not rows for the scaling versions: they measure prompt effects or evaluation-framework performance, not loss scaling. The study also reports that outputs under 500 tokens correlate with higher scores, but this is not a scale comparison.
record.test_reason: The study scores five instruction or reasoning models (32B–671B) on tourism QA and explicitly concludes 'scaling laws persist'. That bears weakly on V6 in a new domain. It fits no scale curve, uses no loss, and confounds size with family, reasoning distillation and quantization (local Q4-K-M versus DS-V3 via API).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors rank DS-V3 > DS-70B > DS-32B > Qwen-72B > Qwen-32B and say scaling laws persist in tourism. They argue reasoning-enhanced sub-72B models significantly beat non-reasoning ones, a pattern reversed on the generic Open LLM Leaderboard. Their main claim concerns the LETToT label-free evaluation framework.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates tourism QA responses with LETToT across selected models; it does not run controlled pretraining-loss sweeps or fit the original scaling-law curves.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and reasoning capability accompany the reported score differences; the paper reports wider score variability for DeepSeek models than for Qwen models.

fits_no_version.finding: At 32B–72B, reasoning-distilled models outscore non-reasoning Qwen models on tourism QA (e.g. DS-32B > Qwen-32B, p=0.045). The ranking reverses relative to the Open LLM Leaderboard.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning distillation, not parameter count, drives domain-specific QA performance at fixed or smaller scale.

record.problems: Only five models are evaluated, with model family and reasoning capability differing alongside size; no scaling curve is fitted. The model-score account is internally inconsistent: the text reports DeepSeek-V3 at 3.47 as the highest, but later calls DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B the highest among the listed models. DeepSeek-V3's size is not assigned in the model specifications.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all separately stated RQ2 mean scores and reported pairwise significance results relevant to downstream performance and scale are recorded.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or power-law fit.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime.
No fitted or predictive relation between scale or loss and score. Five models only, sizes confounded with family, reasoning and quantization.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Stage-1 LLM-judge rankings per dimension, baseline vs optimized. Baseline overall: DS-V3 1st, Qwen-72B 2nd, Qwen-32B 3rd, DS-32B 4th, DS-70B 5th. The larger DS-70B ranks below DS-32B.
AHP dimension scores per model (e.g. DS-32B Rel 6.08 vs DS-V3 4.88; Qwen-72B above Qwen-32B on most dimensions, but not Acc).
Pairwise p-value for Qwen-72B vs Qwen-32B, the only clean within-family size pair, which appears only in the heatmap.
Per-model baseline and optimized mean scores in stage 1.

record.verdict_notes: 'Scaling laws' here means only that the largest model scores highest; there is no fit. Confounds: four local models are Q4-K-M quantized while DS-V3 runs via API; DS-V3 is MoE; the DS-distill pair has different base models. The text internally contradicts itself: Figure 8 discussion calls DS-70B highest 'among listed models' while omitting DS-V3. The dataset is not released.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fits or predictions for larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation or loss-minimising parameter/token split is tested.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study evaluates tourism QA, but does not test whether pretraining-loss power laws transfer to another modality or training regime.
The study reports tourism-task scores across models, but does not fit a predictive scale curve or relate scores to pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
rows.note: A single model score does not establish a scale trend.
rows.check: A single model's score is the reference point, not a scale effect on its own. Qwen-32B was run with Q4-K-M quantization.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct
rows.note: The reported mean is higher than Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct's, but this is a comparison of two models, not a fitted scale relationship.
rows.check: Versus Qwen-32B, the score rises 3.11 vs 2.96. The CIs overlap, and the text reports no p-value for this pair. It is the only clean within-family size comparison.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
rows.note: The reported score is higher than the 32B Qwen model's, but model family and reasoning status differ.
rows.check: A single score. It is the reference for the DS-distill pair, whose base models differ (Qwen vs Llama).

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B
rows.note: The paper separately describes this as the highest score among a listed group, but elsewhere reports DeepSeek-V3 at 3.47 as highest overall.
rows.check: 70B vs 32B distilled scores 3.34 vs 3.30, and the paper reports no significant differences among DS models (p>0.32). The base model differs between the two.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-V3
rows.note: The abstract states that the evaluated models range from 32B to 671B, but does not assign a size to DeepSeek-V3. A later reported hierarchy omits it while calling DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B the highest among the listed models.
rows.check: The largest model (671B per the abstract; MoE, API, not quantized) has the highest mean. Its lead over DS-70B/32B is not significant (R10). Size is not given in Table 1.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-V3 vs Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise t-test of tourism QA performance
rows.note: This comparison shows a difference between models, not a fitted scale effect.
rows.check: A cross-family comparison (671B MoE via API vs a quantized 72B), confounded by family, deployment and quantization. The baseline should read Qwen-72B, not 'not stated' sizes.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-V3 vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise t-test of tourism QA performance
rows.note: This comparison shows a difference between models, not a fitted scale effect.
rows.check: A cross-family comparison confounded as in R6.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise t-test of tourism QA performance
rows.note: This comparison shows a difference between models, not a fitted scale effect.
rows.check: The larger model wins, but it is also a reasoning model of a different family. The authors attribute the gap to reasoning, not scale.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise t-test of tourism QA performance
rows.note: This comparison shows a difference between models, not a fitted scale effect.
rows.check: A same-size (32B vs 32B) reasoning vs non-reasoning comparison; this is not a scale comparison.

rows.subject: DeepSeek models (aggregate)

conditions.value: DeepSeek models compared with one another

rows.value: No significant differences observed among DS models (p >0.32)
rows.note: The text reports the set of DeepSeek pairwise comparisons in aggregate rather than giving separate p-values.
rows.check: No significant score differences among DS models spanning 32B to 671B (p>0.32).

relationships.condition: Largest model (DS-V3, 671B MoE) vs Qwen2.5-32B/72B on the LETToT comprehensive score
relationships.reason: DS-V3 has the highest mean (3.47) and significantly beats Qwen-72B (p=0.019) and Qwen-32B (p=0.0004). This is confounded by family, API deployment and no quantization (R5, R6, R7).
relationships.display_finding: DS-V3 achieved the highest mean of 3.47, exceeding Qwen-72B at p=0.019 and Qwen-32B at p=0.0004, with family, deployment and quantization differences confounding the comparison.

relationships.condition: Within the Qwen2.5 family (32B vs 72B, both Q4 quantized)
relationships.reason: The 72B model scores only slightly higher (3.11 vs 2.96), with overlapping CIs and no significance reported (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: The 72B model scored 3.11 versus 2.96 for 32B, with overlapping confidence intervals and no reported significance.

relationships.reason: The paper reports no significant differences among DS models (p>0.32), so a 20x size span shows no reliable gain (R3, R4, R5, R10).
relationships.display_finding: Performance differences across 32B, 70B and 671B models were nonsignificant, with p>0.32.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported mean scores within the Qwen models and between the two distilled reasoning models
reader_labels.reason: The larger Qwen model has a higher mean than the smaller Qwen model, and the 70B distilled model has a slightly higher mean than the 32B distilled model (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-family model comparisons in tourism QA
reader_labels.reason: Scores are not a clean function of parameter count across model families: the 32B distilled reasoning model scores above the 72B Qwen model, and the study does not fit or validate a predictive scale curve; its reported hierarchy also differs in whether DeepSeek-V3 is included (R1–R5, R8–R10).
